title: Isolation of Neuronal Nuclei From Human Frozen Brain Tissue Using FANS for Methylation Analyses
author: Alexandra Del Favero-Campbell
materials: At this point, you can either freeze the pellet samples at -80 °C for further processing using a Qiagen AllPrep DNA/RNA Micro Kit for simultaneous DNA and RNA extraction (using the Qiagen Manufacturer's Protocol Guidelines ) at a later date. ( Note : This should be done no more than 3 days later.)

Make sure to lubricate the ring around the sheath fluid tank lid with Super O-Lube to get a good seal. Make sure Drop Frequency is set to around 38.9 to 39.2. Try not to adjust this too much. Instead, you can adjust the height of the drops (using the silver knob on the top-right of the machine) and the Piezo Amplitude. Try to keep flow rate at a maximum of 1000 events per second and your efficiency at around 80+ %. Once your Nuclei Sample tube has finished going through the FACSJazz, it can be also very useful to hit the Backflush button and let some sheath fluid run back into the tube. This will release some nuclei that were caught in the tubing system, but did not get analyzed or sorted. You can then hit the Sample button again and analyze these nuclei that were not initially analyzed. You can do this as many times as you want, until you do not see any more nuclei being detected on the monitor. We, generally, repeat this step about 3-5 times to try to get as many nuclei as possible, while also not allowing this to take too much time and contribute to potential sample degradation. 1000x DAPI (1.4uL) can be used in place of Hoechst 33342 dye, if not available. Both dyes have been used and tested in this protocol. However, it can be recommended in some cases, such as when using DAPI, or cases where the spectrums of your chosen fluorescent antibodies overlap, that auto-compensation is performed before performing any gating or sorting. This can be done using this protocol by using the Unstained Control sample as your Negative Control, the Hoechst Control sample as your first single Positive Control, and either Alexa Fluor-488 mixed with UltraComp eBeads (following the bead manufacturer’s protocol) or staining part of the Unstained Control with Alexa Fluor-488 as your second single Positive Control. If for any reason you are not able to perform FANS the same day as your immunostaining procedure, you can dissolve your pellets from Part B, Step #19 in 200uL-1000uL of Bambanker freezing medium using the following steps: Dissolve pellet in 200uL-1000uL of Bambanker freezing medium by allowing pellet to dissolve for a few minutes on ice and then gently pipetting solution up and down gently. Transfer solution to a cryovial and place it in a Mr. Frosty overnight at -80 o C. Store sample at -80 o C for future use and analysis. Make sure to keep wrapped in aluminum foil as they will be photosensitive! In previous testing of protocols using the Qiagen AllPrep Kit, we have found it helpful to incubate both of our DNA and RNA filters in their designated elution buffers for about 3-5 minutes before performing the final centrifugation. For DNA, we elute in 40uL of 64 o C Buffer EB, and for RNA, we elute in 14uL of RNAse-free water. We have also found it useful to perform 2 separate elutions, which can be later combined and further concentrated using a SpeedVac machine.

At this point, you can either freeze the pellet samples at -80 °C for further processing using a Qiagen AllPrep DNA/RNA Micro Kit for simultaneous DNA and RNA extraction (using the Qiagen Manufacturer's Protocol Guidelines ) at a later date. ( Note : This should be done no more than 3 days later.)

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare all necessary materials and pre-chill equipment to maintain a cold environment.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Homogenizing Buffer (HB) and keep on ice.
Pre-chill centrifuge to 4 °C.
Pre-chill homogenizers and pestles on ice.
Place autoclaved forceps and scalpel at -80 °C on dry ice.
Optional: Place a Petri dish on dry ice for chopping tissue.

steps.title: Tissue Homogenization
steps.instruction: Homogenize frozen human brain tissue to isolate nuclei.

substeps.instruction: Weigh approximately 100 mg of sample tissue into Eppendorf tubes (keep at -80 °C on dry ice).
Transfer 100 mg brain chunks to pre-chilled homogenizers on ice using frozen forceps and scalpel.
Add 600 µL of Homogenizing Buffer to each homogenizer.

Wash out the original tissue tubes 3 times using 600 µL of HB per wash (or 1-2 times per tube if multiple tubes were used) to ensure maximum tissue recovery; final volume in homogenizer should be ~2.4 mL.
Lightly wipe the pestle with RNaseZap on a Kimwipe and ensure it is dry.
Administer 30 slow, gentle manual strokes in a beaker of ice, using a grinding motion at the bottom and avoiding lifting the pestle completely to prevent foaming.

steps.title: Filter and Debris Removal
steps.instruction: Filter the homogenate to remove clumps and debris.

substeps.instruction: Check for clumps using a hemocytometer (10 µL sample + 10 µL Trypan Blue); if clumps are visible, perform additional manual strokes.
Filter homogenate through sterile cell strainer caps into a 15 mL Falcon tube on ice using circular movements.
Verify nuclei presence and debris removal via hemocytometer (10 µL sample + 10 µL Trypan Blue).
Repeat the filtration and checking process 1 to 3 times until debris is sufficiently removed.

steps.title: Nuclei Pellet Concentration
steps.instruction: Concentrate the filtered nuclei via centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Evenly split the filtered homogenate into two pre-chilled autoclaved 1.5 mL LoBind Eppendorf tubes on ice.
Centrifuge at 1000 rcf for 8 minutes at 4 °C.
Gently discard supernatant on ice, leaving a small amount of liquid if necessary to avoid disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Iodixanol Gradient Separation
steps.instruction: Use an Iodixanol density gradient to further purify nuclei.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 225 µL of cold HB on ice, then pool the resuspended liquids into a pre-chilled 2 mL LoBind tube (final volume ~450 µL).
Add 450 µL of ice-cold 50% (v/v) Iodixanol to the pooled sample and gently mix by pipetting (final concentration 25% Iodixanol).
Place 900 µL of ice-cold 29% (v/v) Iodixanol into a new pre-chilled 2 mL LoBind tube on ice.
Slowly overlay the 900 µL of 25% Iodixanol/sample solution over the 29% Iodixanol by adding it from the top edge of the tube.
Centrifuge at 13500 rcf for 20 minutes at 4 °C (position tubes with tails facing out).

steps.title: Post-Gradient Recovery
steps.instruction: Recover the nuclei pellet from the gradient.

substeps.instruction: Remove and discard the top myelin-rich debris layer and the aqueous supernatant on ice, keeping the pellet intact.

If performing FANS immediately, proceed to immunostaining. Otherwise, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of 10% DMSO in ice-cold 1x PBS (RNase-free), transfer to a cryovial, and freeze in a Mr. Frosty at -80 °C overnight.

steps.title: Prepare BSA-Coated Tubes
steps.instruction: Prepare tubes for immunostaining one day in advance.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 10% BSA in ice-cold 1x PBS (RNase-free) to autoclaved 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Incubate on ice for 10 minutes.
Rinse with ice-cold 1x PBS (RNase-free) and dry overnight at 4 °C with lids open.
Thaw cryovials completely on ice and gently pipette.
Transfer sample to a pre-chilled 1.5 mL LoBind tube on ice.
Rinse the cryovial with 150 µL of ice-cold 1x PBS (RNase-free) and transfer to the LoBind tube.
Centrifuge at 2050 rcf for 15 minutes at 4 °C and discard supernatant on ice.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL of ice-cold 1x PBS (RNase-free) on ice.
Centrifuge again at 2050 rcf for 15 minutes at 4 °C and discard supernatant on ice.

steps.title: Nuclei Resuspension and Counting
steps.instruction: Dissolve the nuclei pellet and quantify the sample.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL of ice-cold Antibody Incubation Buffer to the pellet and let sit on ice for 20 minutes.
Gently pipette the solution up and down to completely dissolve the pellet.
Transfer the solution to a pre-coated BSA tube on ice, rinsing the original tube with 500 µL of ice-cold 1x PBS (final volume 1 mL).
Count nuclei using a hemocytometer (10 µL sample + 10 µL Trypan Blue). Aliquot the sample if the count is 10 million or more.

steps.title: Immunostaining
steps.instruction: Stain nuclei for NeuN and DNA.

substeps.instruction: Prepare immunostaining mixture on ice: 300 µL 1x RNase-free PBS, 1.2 µL NeuN antibody (clone A60, Alexa Fluor 488), and 100 µL Blocking Mix (0.5% BSA and 10% Normal Goat Serum).
Vortex mixture for 10 seconds and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes in the dark.
Prepare three 1.5 mL LoBind tubes on ice:
Unstained Control: 70 µL nuclei solution + 830 µL 1x PBS (RNase-free).
Hoechst Control: 70 µL nuclei solution + 830 µL 1x PBS (RNase-free).
Nuclei Sample: 860 µL nuclei solution + 140 µL 1x PBS (RNase-free).
Add the immunostaining mixture to the Nuclei Sample tube.
Add 2 µL of Hoechst 33342 (20 mM) to the Hoechst Control and Nuclei Sample tubes.
Rotate samples in the dark at 4 °C for 1.5 to 2 hours.

steps.title: Post-Staining Filtration
steps.instruction: Clean and filter samples before FACS loading.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge samples at 2050 rcf for 5 minutes at 4 °C and discard supernatant on ice.
Gently pipette the sample up and down with a P1000.
Filter the sample through a 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom tube with a cell-strainer cap on ice.
Transfer the filtered sample to a polypropylene 5 mL tube covered in aluminum foil and keep on ice.
Lightly vortex at the lowest setting for 10-30 seconds immediately before loading into the FACS chamber.

steps.title: FANS Collection Tube Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare tubes for sorted nuclei one day prior.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL ice-cold 1x PBS (RNase-free), 25 µL RNAse Inhibitor (40 U/µL), and 500 µL 10% BSA to pre-chilled 1.5 mL LoBind tubes (at least 2-4 tubes per sample for NeuN+ and NeuN-).
Invert gently and incubate on ice for 10 minutes.
Rinse with 1 mL ice-cold 1x PBS (RNase-free) and dry overnight at 4 °C with lids open.

steps.title: FACS Machine Setup
steps.instruction: Configure the BD FACSJazz for nuclei sorting.

substeps.instruction: Ensure 6 L of filtered, autoclaved 1x sheath fluid is at room temperature (~23 °C).
Set the cooling system to 5 °C.
Set PMTs, FSC, and SSC to log-scale (optional for FSC/SSC); set key threshold to FSC at ~1.65.
Adjust Sample Offset to achieve ~200 events per second.

steps.title: Gating and Sorting
steps.instruction: Perform sequential gating to isolate NeuN+ and NeuN- nuclei.

substeps.instruction: Run Unstained Control: Use SSC vs. FSC to create a 'Cells' gate (exclude debris) and Trigger Pulse Width vs. FSC to create a 'Singlets' gate (exclude doublets).
Run Hoechst Control: Use 520/35[405] vs. 450/50[405] to create a 'Nuclei' gate. Double-check using 450/50[405] vs. FSC to ensure single nuclei are captured.

Run Nuclei Sample: Use 530/40[488] vs. 450/50[405] to create 'NeuN positive' (high y-axis, high x-axis) and 'NeuN negative' (low y-axis, high x-axis) gates. If differentiation is difficult, use a cutoff just above 10² on the y-axis.
Set Sort Mode to 1.0 Drop Enrich and set both NeuN+ and NeuN- gates to 'Unlimited'.
Start sort and maintain event rate at 100-300 events per second (Sample Offset typically 0.15 to 0.17 psi).
Monitor droplet breakoff point and flickers of light to ensure proper deflection into collection tubes.

steps.title: Post-Sort Recovery and Storage
steps.instruction: Process sorted nuclei for final analysis or storage.

substeps.instruction: Remove collection tubes and place immediately on ice.
Perform machine shutdown (Wet or Dry).
Visually inspect final volume of NeuN+ and NeuN- tubes and add reagents based on volume (round up):
- For 500 µL: 100 µL 1.8M Sucrose, 2.5 µL 1M CaCl2, 1.5 µL 1M Mg(Ac)2.
- For 1.0 mL: 200 µL 1.8M Sucrose, 5 µL 1M CaCl2, 3 µL 1M Mg(Ac)2.
- For 1.5 mL: 300 µL 1.8M Sucrose, 7.5 µL 1M CaCl2, 4.5 µL 1M Mg(Ac)2.
Mix gently by inverting and incubate on ice for 15 minutes.
Centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 15 minutes at 4 °C and carefully discard supernatant on ice.
For long-term storage: Dissolve pellet in 200 µL Bambanker freezing medium on ice, transfer to cryovial, and store in Mr. Frosty at -80 °C overnight.
